claim: AWS WAF can protect websites not hosted in AWS, because it is integrated with Amazon CloudFront, which supports custom origins outside of AWS.
question: Can AWS WAF protect a website that runs in an on-premises data center?

values.display: supports custom origins outside of AWS
integrated with Amazon CloudFront

qualifiers.condition: the site is served through a CloudFront distribution

evidence.quote: Yes, AWS WAF is integrated with Amazon CloudFront, which supports custom origins outside of AWS.

note: d006. FAQ question: 'Can I use AWS WAF to protect web sites not hosted in AWS?'

claim: When you use AWS WAF on CloudFront, your rules run in all AWS edge locations close to end users, and blocked requests are stopped before they reach your web servers; on regional services such as ALB, API Gateway and AppSync, rules run in the Region and can protect internet-facing and internal resources.
question: Where do AWS WAF rules run for a CloudFront distribution compared with an ALB?

values.display: your rules run in all AWS Edge Locations
Blocked requests are stopped before they reach your web servers.
your rules run in region

evidence.quote: When you use AWS WAF on Amazon CloudFront, your rules run in all AWS Edge Locations, located around the world close to your end users. This means security doesn’t come at the expense of performance. Blocked requests are stopped before they reach your web servers. When you use AWS WAF on regional services, such as Application Load Balancer, Amazon API Gateway, and AWS AppSync, your rules run in region and can be used to protect internet-facing resources as well as internal resources.

claim: The underlying service forwards the requests it receives to AWS WAF for inspection, and AWS WAF then instructs that service to block or allow each request based on the action you define.
question: Which component actually blocks a request that AWS WAF rejects?

values.display: it forwards those requests to AWS WAF for inspection
AWS WAF instructs the underlying service to either block or allow

evidence.quote: As the underlying service receives requests for your web sites, it forwards those requests to AWS WAF for inspection against your rules. Once a request meets a condition defined in your rules, AWS WAF instructs the underlying service to either block or allow the request based on the action you define.

claim: For CloudFront standard distributions, AWS WAF adds protection with a single web ACL for each distribution, and you can enable it by associating an existing web ACL or with one-click protection in the CloudFront console.
question: How do you turn on AWS WAF for a CloudFront distribution?

values.display: using a single protection pack (web ACL) for each distribution
by using one-click protection in the CloudFront console

evidence.quote: For standard distributions, AWS WAF adds protection using a single protection pack (web ACL) for each distribution. You can enable this protection by associating an existing protection pack (web ACL) with a CloudFront distribution or by using one-click protection in the CloudFront console.

unless you switch back to pay-as-you-go pricing

evidence.quote: A valid AWS WAF protection pack (web ACL) must remain associated with your CloudFront distribution when using any pricing plan. You cannot remove the protection pack (web ACL) association unless you switch back to pay-as-you-go pricing.

claim: When a web ACL protects an Application Load Balancer that is the origin of a CloudFront distribution, you must configure CloudFront to forward the aws-waf-token cookie, because by default CloudFront removes cookies before forwarding a request to the origin.
question: What extra configuration do CAPTCHA and Challenge tokens need when the ALB with the web ACL sits behind CloudFront?

values.display: CloudFront removes cookies from the web request
To keep the token cookie with the web request

qualifiers.scope: web ACL on an ALB that is a CloudFront origin
qualifiers.condition: rules that use tokens (CAPTCHA, Challenge, intelligent threat mitigation)

evidence.quote: By default, CloudFront removes cookies from the web request before forwarding it to the origin. To keep the token cookie with the web request, configure CloudFront cache behavior to include either just the token cookie or all cookies.

note: d007. Page title: 'Required configuration for Application Load Balancers that are CloudFront origins'. The page does not discuss stopping clients that bypass CloudFront.

claim: For a Block action you can define a custom response with a status code, headers and a response body, and you can redirect the client by using a 3xx status code with a Location header.
question: Can AWS WAF send a custom error page or redirect instead of a plain 403?

values.display: you define the status code, headers, and response body
Redirecting the client to a different URL.

qualifiers.scope: Block rule actions and Block default actions

evidence.quote: When you define custom response handling for a Block action, you define the status code, headers, and response body.

Redirecting the client to a different URL. To do this, you specify one of the `3xx` redirection status codes, like `301 (Moved Permanently)` or `302 (Found)`, and then specify a new header named `Location` with the new URL.

claim: Custom responses that you specify for the AWS WAF Block action take precedence over any response specifications defined in the protected resource.

evidence.quote: Custom responses that you specify for the AWS WAF Block action take precedence over any response specifications that you define in your protected resource.
